steps.text: An app is any program on your comptuer that you can run to perform a specific function. This includes File Explorer, a browser like Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome, text editors like Microsoft Word or Notepad, and more. There three main ways to open an app that we will explore in this lesson.
steps.hintText: When you're done reading, click Next to continue.

steps.text: The first way you can open an app is through your taskbar, the row of app icons at the bottom of your screen. Open the File Explorer app by clicking on the folder icon in the taskbar. This will open a window that allows you to navigate through your files and folders.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder icon in the taskbar at the bottom of your screen and click on it to open File Explorer.

steps.text: Great job! Now click the 'X' in the top right corner of the File Explorer window to close it.
steps.hintText: Look for the 'X' in the top right corner of the File Explorer window and click on it to close the app.

steps.text: The next way you can open an app is by clicking on app icons on your desktop. If you have a shortcut to an app on your desktop, you can double click the icon to open it. Try opening File Explorer again by double clicking the folder icon on your desktop.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder icon on your desktop and double click on it to open File Explorer.

steps.text: Perfect! Now close the File Explorer window again by clicking the 'X' in the top right corner.
steps.hintText: Look for the 'X' in the top right corner of the File Explorer window and click on it to close the app.

steps.text: The third way you can open an app is through the start menu. Click on the windows button in the taskbar at the bottom of your screen to open the start menu.
steps.hintText: Look for the windows button in the taskbar at the bottom of your screen and click on it to open the start menu.

steps.text: The start menu contains a list of all the apps on your computer. You can scroll through the list to find the app you want to open, or you can use the search bar at the top of the start menu to quickly find an app by typing its name. (Press Next to continue)
steps.hintText: Take some time to explore the start menu and see all the apps that are on your computer. When you're ready, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Try opening the File Explorer again by clicking on the folder icon in the start menu.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder icon in the start menu and click on it to open File Explorer.

steps.text: Awesome! Now close the File Explorer window one last time by clicking the 'X' in the top right corner.
steps.hintText: Look for the 'X' in the top right corner of the File Explorer window and click on it to close the app.

steps.text: Congratulations! You've learned how to open apps on your computer through the taskbar, desktop icons, and the start menu.
steps.hintText: Great job! You've completed the lesson on opening apps. You can try opening any app on your computer using any of the methods we covered in this lesson. When you're ready, press Finish to end the lesson.

steps.text: Start by opening the Notepad app by double-clicking the Desktop icon with "Notepad" under it.
steps.hintText: Look for the icon on your desktop that has a notepad icon and says "Notepad" under it. Double click on that icon to open the Notepad app. Make sure to open the Notepad app through the Desktop.

steps.text: The Notepad app is a basic text editor that lets you write and edit plain text. You can use it to take notes, write lists, or even write code!
steps.hintText: When you finish reading, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Try clicking on the text area in the notepad app and typing some text in. The app has some example text to start, which you can also edit or delete.
steps.hintText: You can type anything you want in the Notepad app, and click Next when you're done.

steps.text: In Notepad, as well as in many other apps like your web browser, you can click and drag across text to select it. Try it out by clicking and dragging across some text to see it outlined, then hit Next when you're done.
steps.hintText: You can select and drag around as much or as little text as you want. When you're done, click Next.

steps.text: Now try highlighting some text and hitting Ctrl and C on your keyboard at the same time to copy the text. This saves a copy of the text to your clipboard, which is a special area of your computer's memory that can hold text or images that you've copied or cut.
steps.hintText: Highlight some text by clicking and dragging across it, then press Ctrl and C on your keyboard at the same time to copy the text.

steps.text: Now try pressing Ctrl and V on your keyboard at the same time to paste the text. This pastes the text from your clipboard into the current document.
steps.hintText: Press Ctrl and V on your keyboard at the same time to paste the text you copied back into the notepad editor.

steps.text: Now highlight some text and press Ctrl and X on your keyboard at the same time to cut the text. This removes the text from your document and saves it to your clipboard, so you can paste it somewhere else if you want.
steps.hintText: Highlight some text by clicking and dragging across it, then press Ctrl and X on your keyboard at the same time to cut the text.

steps.text: Press Ctrl and V to paste the text you cut back into the notepad editor.
steps.hintText: Press Ctrl and V on your keyboard at the same time to paste the text you cut back into the notepad editor.

steps.text: Good job! You've learned how to select text and use the copy, cut, and paste functions in Notepad. These functions work in many other apps as well, so you can use them to easily move or copy text around on your computer.
steps.hintText: Congratulations! You've completed the lesson on using Notepad. You can continue to copy, cut, and paste text in the Notepad app. When you are done, press Finish.

steps.text: The file explorer allows you to see every file that you have on your computer. This includes applications, downloaded files, documents, and even system files. Start by opening the file explorer.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder icon on your desktop and double click on it to open File Explorer. Be sure to open the File Explorer app through the Desktop.

steps.text: When you first open the app, you see the Quick Access menu. As you can see, it shows shortcuts to commonly accessed folders like Documents or Pictures.
steps.hintText: Once you're done exploring the Quick Access menu, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Click on the Desktop folder on the left to go to the desktop folder.
steps.hintText: Look for the Desktop folder in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the desktop folder.

steps.text: In the desktop folder, you can see all the files that are on the desktop. Right now, it only has shortcuts to 3 apps, but you can place any files on the desktop and their icons will be easily accessible.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the desktop folder and see the files that are on your desktop, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now click on the Downloads folder on the left.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Downloads in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the downloads folder.

steps.text: In the downloads folder, you can see all the files that you have downloaded to your computer. By default, most web browsers will save downloaded files to this folder, so it's a good place to check when you download something from the internet.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the downloads folder and see the files, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now click on the Documents folder on the left.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Documents in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the documents folder.

steps.text: In the documents folder, you can see all the files that you have created or saved in your Documents folder. This is a good place to keep your personal files like word documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the documents folder and see the files, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now click on the Pictures folder on the left.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Pictures in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the pictures folder.

steps.text: In the pictures folder, you can see all the images that you have saved to your computer. This is the default location for screenshots, pictures uploaded from the phone, and pictures applications might save.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the pictures folder and see the files, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now click on the Music folder on the left.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Music in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the music folder.

steps.text: The music folder is where music is saved to your computer. If you download music or import it from a device, this is where it will be saved.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the music folder and see the files, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now click on the Videos folder on the left.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Videos in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the videos folder.

steps.text: The videos folder is where videos are saved to your computer. If you record something on your screen, this is where the default location for videos will be.
steps.hintText: When you're done exploring the videos folder and see the files, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Now go back to the documents folder so we can try to create our own folder.
steps.hintText: Look for the folder labeled Documents in the left sidebar of the File Explorer window and click on it to open the documents folder.

steps.text: Click "New" in the top left, and then click "Folder" to create a new folder.
steps.hintText: Look for the "New" button in the top left of the File Explorer window, click on it, and then click on "Folder" to create a new folder.

steps.text: And that is the end of this lesson! You've learned how to navigate through the file explorer and find important folders on your computer. You also learned how to create a new folder to organize your files. Great job!
steps.hintText: Congratulations! You've completed the lesson on using the File Explorer. You can continue to explore the File Explorer and navigate through your files and folders. When you're done, click Finish to end the lesson.

steps.text: For this lesson, we will be using the Notepad app. Open the Notepad app from the Desktop.
steps.hintText: Look for the icon on your desktop that has a notepad icon and says "Notepad" under it. Double click on that icon to open the Notepad app. Make sure to open the Notepad app through the Desktop.

steps.text: Like in the copy, cut, and paste lesson, we will be using keyboard shortcuts to perform different functions in the Notepad app. Keyboard shortcuts are combinations of keys that you can press to quickly perform a function without having to click through menus. For example, Ctrl and C is the keyboard shortcut for copy, and Ctrl and V is the keyboard shortcut for paste.
steps.hintText: When you're done reading, click Next to continue.

steps.text: Try pressing Ctrl and A on your keyboard at the same time to select all the text in the document. This is a common keyboard shortcut that works in many apps to select all the text or items in a document or folder.
steps.hintText: Press the Ctrl key and the A key on your keyboard at the same time to select all the text in the notepad document.
